title: Real world MCPs in GitHub Copilot Agent Mode — Jon Peck, Microsoft

primary.label: Tools, Protocols & Integrations

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The central subject is MCP (Model Context Protocol), an open protocol for connecting LLMs to external data and tools, matching this category's defining example. GitHub Copilot is a coding assistant, and MCP servers are developer-platform integration tools used by software builders. Demonstrations span development (app building), testing (mock data generation), and production-adjacent enterprise workflows (repo settings, autonomous agents). Assumes familiarity with VS Code, GitHub, and databases but remains accessible to practicing developers. Conference talk structured around live demonstrations of MCP configuration and usage within Copilot agent mode. Multiple transcript evidence anchors with specific excerpts directly support the MCP-focused classification.

summary: Jon Peck (Microsoft) presents how GitHub Copilot's agent mode, enhanced by MCPs, addresses real engineering problems beyond prototype 'vibe-coding.' He traces Copilot's evolution: from micro-level code completion, to one-shot chat interactions, to agent mode—deep, interactive sessions where the agent builds complete applications or performs large refactorings. He demonstrates agent mode building a travel reservation app from a README in about 8 minutes, with the agent requesting terminal permissions and reacting to errors. Peck introduces MCP (Model Context Protocol) as an open protocol—an API for AI—enabling LLMs to connect to external data sources, references, and tools. Mechanically, the IDE (VS Code) is configured with desired MCPs; Copilot selects the appropriate MCP for a task and connects either locally or via SSE to remote servers. Thousands of MCP servers are available. A Postgres MCP demonstration shows one-click VS Code configuration, filling in a connection string, and starting the server. Peck explicitly instructs Copilot to use the Postgres MCP to pull data and create a mock.json for test building, highlighting that this MCP operates in readonly mode to prevent accidental mutations. The workflow involves Copilot parsing the prompt, requesting developer permission, handshaking with the MCP to get schema, select tables, and pull data, then integrating results into context. Peck also introduces GitHub's own MCP server, authenticated via personal access token, enabling account-specific operations including committing changes to a new branch and creating a PR in a single step. He shares a best practice: using a .github/copilot-instructions.md file to pre-inject standards (PEP 8, security checks, changelog generation) into every prompt. He emphasizes first prompts are rarely correct, advocating iterative refinement. During Q&A, Peck describes GitHub.com's assign-issue-to-Copilot feature, where Copilot works autonomously in the background on assigned issues, producing PRs with viewable sessions. He notes enterprise versus independent developer concerns may keep this as a separate workflow for now, and that MCP can be configured in repo settings under the Copilot subset for this feature as well. A references slide at gh.io/fair/mcp provides links to VS Code and MCP installation resources.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Copilot Evolution: Code Completion to Agent Mode
sections.summary: Peck traces Copilot's progression from micro-level code completion, to one-shot chat interactions, to agent mode for complete tasks with deep interaction, including building greenfield apps and large refactoring.

sections.title: Agent Mode Demo: Building from README
sections.summary: Demonstrates agent mode building a travel reservation app from a README containing project structure, environment config, database schema, and API endpoints, including workflow graphs as images or mermaid diagrams. The app was built in about 8 minutes with terminal permission prompts.

sections.title: Introduction to MCP
sections.summary: Introduces MCP (Model Context Protocol) as an open protocol—an API for AI—allowing LLMs to connect to external data sources and references. Notes thousands of MCP servers exist at github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers.

sections.title: MCP Mechanics and Configuration
sections.summary: Explains how MCPs work mechanically: IDE configures desired MCPs, Copilot selects the right one for a task, connects locally or via SSE to remote servers. Demonstrates one-click VS Code configuration and the tools icon for viewing enabled MCP servers.

sections.title: Postgres MCP Demonstration
sections.summary: Demonstrates adding a Postgres MCP server via one-click config, filling in a connection string, starting the server, and explicitly instructing Copilot to use it. The MCP operates in readonly mode for safety. Copilot pulls data and creates a mock.json for test building, requiring permission for database connections.

sections.title: MCP Workflow Mechanics
sections.summary: Details the mechanical workflow: Copilot parses the prompt, identifies the MCP, requests developer permission, handshakes with the MCP (get schema, select tables, pull data), parses responses, creates output files, and adds results to context for successive work. Emphasizes iterative prompting.

sections.title: GitHub MCP Server and Best Practices
sections.summary: Introduces GitHub's own MCP server authenticated via personal access token for account-specific operations. Shares best practice of using .github/copilot-instructions.md to pre-inject standards (PEP 8, security checks, changelog generation) into every prompt for consistent agent behavior.

sections.title: GitHub MCP for Branch and PR Creation
sections.summary: Demonstrates using the GitHub MCP in a single step to commit changes to a new branch and create a PR, replacing manual git commands or VS Code interactions. Copilot requests permission to make the connection, create the branch, and create the PR.

sections.title: References and Q&A: Assign Issue to Copilot
sections.summary: Shares references slide at gh.io/fair/mcp with links to VS Code and MCP installation resources. Q&A covers GitHub.com's assign-issue-to-Copilot feature where Copilot works autonomously in the background on assigned issues, producing PRs with viewable sessions. Peck notes enterprise versus independent developer concerns may keep this as a separate workflow, and that MCP is configurable in repo settings under the Copilot subset for this feature.
